verdict.tagline: Endless leaf-blowing progression with deep layers of prestige mechanics.

you want a free game with no forced purchases

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the text and UI elements are too small and low-resolution, making them difficult to read.

citations.review_text: Does not scale resolution and no resolution settings in options, this means text is blurry and pixel art has weird artifacts making the game entirely unplayable as looking for more than a couple minutes gives me a headache

I saw this game "advertised" in reviews for a different game that I enjoy, so I came to see why this game was "better" than the other game.   I am quite disappointed.

I won't mention the other game, as a courtesy to this dev, but comparing "Leaf-Blower Revolution" to the other game is like comparing the original DOOM with the newer DOOM: ETERNAL.

I'm no fan of 8-bit or pixel graphics, and LBR has those.  First disappointment.   The text is also in krappy, lo-res, 8bit graphics and I cant decipher most of it.

As of this review, I've only played 20 minutes, and I'll likely play more to see if things improve, but....

- I have robot assistants that... have to stop and recharge every few seconds? Disappointing.

- I have a RAKE that... blows leaves away? Seriously? A rake should pull them towards me. Acenine.

- The "blown" leaves just ... vanish into thin air? Maybe I can make that happen in real life.... I do have a leaf-blower that becomes a vacuum so I can vacuum up the leaves and turn them into mulch.... but that pulls them in, not blowing them away. ... I also have several rakes that all .... fail to "blow" leaves away... so maybe there's a way to change them to be more like the game?

The best thing I can say for the game are these things:
1 - it's free.
2 - it's free.
3 - it's free.
4 - it's free.
5 - it is free
6 - it's free....it is
7 - it's m-f'ing free.
8 - Plays on Win-7
9 - plays on linux
10 - in case you missed it.... it's free.

1 leaf out of 10 possible.

Now, I got a yard full of leaves I gotta go rake in real life.
I hope the font will be larger.
UI and text are too small. for me unplayable.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience display and window management issues where the game fails to properly scale or stay in fullscreen mode, causing mouse input to drift off the game area onto the desktop.

citations.review_text:
This game is great, but there is a game breaking bug that I ran into. If your monitor/pc goes into sleep mode while you are afk (Screen goes black after a certain time) the game will break and enter this strange border-less mini screen mode by itself. You can't click anything that isn't in the top right corner of the screen and you can't save and exit the game because your mouse will just drift off the screen and onto your desktop. You have the shut down the game manually through steam or tm to close it.

Otherwise this game is really awesome so far, no other issues, great time killer.

can someone tell me why the game doesn't fullscreen? whenever i start it, it's small and my mouse isn't always fully connected to the game, like once i reach halfway to the start new game button my mouse goes off the game and i can't play
it wont let me full screen it.
You can't exit fullscreen, despite the option in game, it does not work, and it is fixed onto whatever monitor steam decides.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the gameplay progression as featuring multiple upgrade systems, equipment unlocks, and prestige mechanics.

citations.review_text:
Leaf Blower Revolution is a free idle game built around one of the most ridiculous ideas we can think of, blowing leaves. We start off doing it ourselves with a basic blower, but pretty quickly the game turns into a much bigger progression system with better equipment, upgrades, automation and loads of different areas to unlock. What starts as a joke actually turns into a surprisingly deep idle game.

The best part is the progression. We can buy better blowers, unlock autoblowers and keep improving how quickly we collect leaves. Eventually we are not really blowing anything ourselves anymore because most of the work has been automated. Watching everything start working together and seeing the numbers get bigger is what makes the game so addictive.

There is also a ridiculous amount of stuff to unlock. There are more than 40 areas, over 30 types of leaves, more than 38 shops and dozens of pets. We also get special leaves, crafting, fruits and a load of different upgrade systems. The game keeps introducing new things long after the basic leaf blowing idea has stopped being new.

The prestige system is another important part of it. We can reset parts of our progress to get permanent bonuses and then build everything back up much faster. This works really well for an idle game because even when we reset, it does not feel like all our progress was pointless. We are basically setting ourselves up to reach further the next time.

I also like how much we can do while being completely idle. We can leave the game running while doing something else, come back later and have loads of resources waiting for us. At the same time, there are active things we can do when we actually want to play, so it does not force us to choose between being completely idle or constantly clicking.

The biggest problem is that the amount of systems can get overwhelming. There are so many currencies, areas, upgrades, pets and different mechanics that it can take a while to understand what we are actu…

Leaf Blower Revolution is deceptively simple, but somehow it keeps you coming back far longer than you’d expect. On the surface, it’s just an idle game where you blow leaves and upgrade your blower....but the little touches make it genuinely satisfying.

There’s something almost therapeutic about watching your numbers grow, unlocking new equipment, and seeing progress happen almost automatically. It scratches that oddly addictive itch that only idle games seem to hit perfectly. Upgrading your blower, unlocking new areas, and watching your “leaf empire” expand gives a tiny but consistent sense of achievement.

The game doesn’t try to be anything it isn’t, and that honesty works in its favour. It’s light-hearted, a bit silly, and never pretentious. The humour sneaks in through little details, the animations are simple but charming, and there’s a subtle joy in seeing just how far you can push your blower upgrades.

Even as an idle game, it manages to keep you engaged. You’ll find yourself checking in, tweaking upgrades, and planning your next big leaf-blowing session longer than you expected. It’s relaxing without being boring, and that’s a rare balance to strike

Final Rating: 7.1 / 10

Simple, satisfying, and surprisingly addictive. A small game that punches above its weight in fun

Игра Leaf Blower Revolution - Idle Game - это на удивление затягивающая "кликалка". Вначале кажется, что это просто бессмысленное дуновение на листики, но постепенно открывается многослойная система улучшений, престижа и новых механик.

Очаровательная пиксельная графика и непринуждённый юмор добавляют шарма, делая игру приятной даже во время самых монотонных моментов. Постоянно есть ощущение прогресса, будь то разблокировка новой зоны, улучшение оборудования или получение престижных наград.

Система достижений и скрытых секретов мотивирует исследовать каждый уголок игры, а множество стратегий оптимизации заставляет поломать голову над эффективностью "выдувания" листьев. Несмотря на жанр "idle", игра требует определённого внимания, особенно на ранних этапах, чтобы эффективно использовать доступные ресурсы.

Идеально подходит для коротких сессий, когда хочется просто расслабиться и посмотреть, как цифры растут. Рекомендую всем любителям жанра и тем, кто ищет простую, но увлекательную игру на "пощелкать".

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: The free structure appeals immediately, though rapid mechanic introductions and sudden pacing shifts overwhelm players.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as free, noting that support packs are not required to play.

citations.review_text: Can't compare to other idle games, since I haven't played any, but it did stunt me when I discovered it is free, and you really don't need to buy the support packs to play. After Big Leaf crunch, the returns diminish drastically though and I don't know if I am just not noticing a crucial option hidden in the walls of upgrades, or this is how its meant to be played. What I am trying to say is, sometimes it feels overwhelming and you are not really told what to do exactly.

This is more of a neutral review that leans positive. Leaf Blower Revolution is an incremental game with a lot of depth, but the execution is slightly lacking in terms of design and UI. The game starts off really fun, with upgrades and a pretty seamless path forward. However, after you hit Big Leaf Crunch, the game pacing slows to a crawl, with little to do to speed it up other than to just wait. I didn't want to go through this hump, so I stopped after BLCing multiple times. Certain UI aspects also were a little underdeveloped and slightly frustrating.

Also I had issues launching the game. I eventually figured out that it was probably some Steam Cloud save issue. I disabled cloud save on launch and the game was able to launch.

All in all, not a bad game, especially since it is free.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game causes hardware strain, specifically noting that it makes computer fans spin up or causes systems to struggle.

citations.review_text:
Idler games are supposed to require very little interaction from the player, yet give a sense of progression.
After maybe a couple of weeks, there has been no progress whatsoever. It feels like I'd have to let the game run and actually spend time on it to move forward.

I won't, that's what actual games are for. I'm even less inclined given how much resources it wastes (It makes the fans spin up. Even beautiful games don't do that on this machine.)

After two months mindlessly starting the game to collect "dailies" before closing it, I'm calling it: it's not worth it.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players enjoy layered prestige mechanics completely free, relying heavily on external guides.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features multiple layers of prestige systems, including meta-prestige mechanics.

citations.review_text:
Ok that was a fun game with a lot of stuff. A LOT. For example there is a prestige system. Nothing new, all idlers have it. But how about meta-prestige, when you clear not only current run but all prestige bonuses. Aaaand guess what - game has even meta-meta-prestige. And it's only the beginning. 

It's so much of everything that I felt overwhelmed at some point. I drew a line at crafting system where you need to craft several set of leafs for different situations with GREAT impact or RNG.

I've put many hours into this game, the bulk of that letting it idle overnight. The gameplay starts off basic and slow, with a LOT of different mechanics added over time as you go further into it. You can easily lose yourself in trying to optimize this thing.

It's a solid idle game, 10/10 would blow leaves again.

As I blow leaves my mind is free, this game is the greatest idle game ever created and i've done many. But this game is made for blower fanatics, while the early game and the "late" game are well paced the mid game will play with your sanity, the pyramid will break you. 
The gameplay is very profound to the point where the wiki is mandatory to save thousands of hours of wrong  choices. But optimising the card, craft, equipement, pets or unique leaves is somewhat rewarding though you will lose hours of your life. 
I recommend this game to any player at least for the amazing early game that doesn't feel like an idle game
